q1:
Bug: `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` returns a 500 instead of a validation error when the body sets `title` to null.
- Repro: create an item, then `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` with `{"title": null}`. `ItemUpdate` in `backend/app/models.py` accepts the null. `update_item` in `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` then copies it onto the row through `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` and `sqlmodel_update`, and the commit fails on the non-null `title` column.
- Same pattern in `PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}`: `UserUpdate` allows `email`, `is_active` and `is_superuser` to be null. `update_user` only checks `if user_in.email:` and `crud.update_user` writes the nulls through.
- Explicit nulls on non-nullable fields must be rejected with a 422 before anything reaches the session.
- `description` (items) and `full_name` (users) must stay clearable by sending null. This is a product decision; don't change it.
- The `ItemPublic` and `UserPublic` response models must stay unchanged.
Acceptance: new cases in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py` and `backend/tests/api/routes/test_users.py` cover the null-title, null-email and cleared-description/full_name paths. All existing tests in `backend/tests/api/routes/` pass unchanged.
q2: Fix the FastAPI/SQLModel `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` and `PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}` endpoints so explicit nulls on non-nullable fields (`title`, `email`, `is_active`, `is_superuser`) in `ItemUpdate`/`UserUpdate` in `backend/app/models.py` are rejected with a 422 instead of a 500, while `description` and `full_name` stay clearable, adding tests in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py` and `test_users.py`.
q3: Reject explicit nulls on non-nullable fields with a 422 in item and user update endpoints, while keeping description and full_name clearable.
FastAPI with SQLModel/Pydantic models, `backend/app/models.py`, `backend/app/api/routes/items.py`, `backend/app/api/routes/users.py`, and tests in `backend/tests/api/routes/`.

q1: In the frontend, any 403 from the API logs the user out. `handleApiError` in `frontend/src/main.tsx` clears `access_token` and redirects to `/login` for both 401 and 403. Ordinary permission errors therefore act like an expired session. One example is "Not enough permissions" from the items routes. Another is a superuser hitting Delete in `frontend/src/components/UserSettings/DeleteConfirmation.tsx`, which gets "Super users are not allowed to delete themselves". In both cases the user is kicked to the login page instead of seeing the error toast. The backend's real invalid-token case is the 403 with detail "Could not validate credentials" raised in `get_current_user` (`backend/app/api/deps.py`). Keep the diff minimal: only log out on 401 or on that specific credentials 403, and let every other 403 fall through to the existing `handleError` toast. Add no new packages, and don't touch the generated client in `frontend/src/client`.
q2: Change `handleApiError` in the React frontend's `frontend/src/main.tsx` so it only clears `access_token` and redirects to `/login` on a 401 or a 403 with detail "Could not validate credentials", letting other 403s fall through to the existing `handleError` toast.
q3: Frontend API error handling that logs out only on 401 or the invalid-credentials 403, and shows an error toast for other permission 403s.
Minimal diff with no new packages, and leave the generated client untouched.

q1: 아이템 title/description으로 우선순위를 분류하는 모델이 아직 없어서 새로 만들어 주세요. 모델은 `backend/app/ml/item_classifier.py`에 만들고, 학습 데이터도 없으니 `backend/app/ml/data/`에 샘플 데이터셋을 같이 만들어 주세요. 데이터셋은 '긴급' 라벨이 아주 적은 불균형 데이터로 구성하면 돼요. 기본 학습 버전과 class weight 또는 focal loss를 넣은 버전을 각각 학습하고, 클래스별 F1을 비교해 주세요.
q2: Create a Python item-priority classifier from title/description in `backend/app/ml/item_classifier.py` with an imbalanced sample dataset (few 'urgent' labels) in `backend/app/ml/data/`, then train a baseline and a class-weighted or focal-loss version and compare per-class F1.
q3: Item priority text classifier trained on title and description, using an imbalanced sample dataset with a rare 'urgent' label, comparing per-class F1 for a baseline against class-weighted or focal-loss training.
Python ML module in `backend/app/ml/item_classifier.py` with a sample dataset in `backend/app/ml/data/`.

q1: 아이템 클릭률(CTR) 예측 서빙 코드를 `backend/app/ml/ctr.py`에 새로 만들어 주세요. 학습 config도 아직 없으니 `backend/app/ml/ctr_config.json`으로 같이 만들어 주세요. 피처 해싱 버킷 수가 학습 때와 다르면 예측값이 전부 0.5 근처로 나오기 때문에, 버킷 수는 하드코딩하지 말고 이 config에서 읽어오게 해 주세요. 불일치하면 `backend/app/main.py`에서 앱이 시작할 때 에러가 나게 해 주세요.
q2: Create Python CTR prediction serving code in `backend/app/ml/ctr.py` that reads the feature-hashing bucket count from a new `backend/app/ml/ctr_config.json`, and make the FastAPI app in `backend/app/main.py` fail at startup on a bucket-count mismatch.
q3: Item click-through-rate (CTR) prediction serving that reads its feature-hashing bucket count from a training config and fails at app startup on a mismatch.

q1: `pages/users/[id].tsx`에 TensorFlow.js로 사용자 프로필 사진 분류를 붙이려고 해요. 아직 관련 코드가 전혀 없으니 `@tensorflow/tfjs`를 `package.json`에 추가하고, 전처리 함수를 `utils/preprocess.ts`에 새로 만들어 주세요. 2D 드로잉 표면(HTML 그리기 요소)에서 픽셀을 읽을 때 RGB/BGR 순서와 정규화가 브라우저마다 달라지지 않게 해서, Safari와 Chrome에서 같은 입력 텐서가 나오도록 해 주세요.
q2: Add `@tensorflow/tfjs` to `package.json` and create a preprocessing function in `utils/preprocess.ts` for profile-photo classification in the React/Next.js page `pages/users/[id].tsx`, ensuring pixels read from a 2D canvas produce identical channel order and normalization in Safari and Chrome.
q3: Profile photo classification with TensorFlow.js, using canvas pixel preprocessing that keeps channel order and normalization consistent so Safari and Chrome produce identical input tensors.

q1: Two kinds of JWT are signed with the same `SECRET_KEY` and `HS256`: access tokens from `create_access_token` in `backend/app/core/security.py`, and password-reset tokens from `generate_password_reset_token` in `backend/app/utils.py`. Neither carries a token-type claim. As a result, each kind decodes successfully wherever the other is expected, and only the `sub` lookup happens to fail. Please harden this: add a type claim to both, and make `get_current_user` in `backend/app/api/deps.py` and `verify_password_reset_token` reject tokens of the wrong type. Keep the diff minimal and don't change any function signatures, because the routes in `login.py` and `users.py` and the helpers in `backend/tests/utils/` call them by name.
q2: Add a token-type claim to the PyJWT access tokens from `create_access_token` in `backend/app/core/security.py` and password-reset tokens from `generate_password_reset_token` in `backend/app/utils.py`, and make `get_current_user` in `backend/app/api/deps.py` and `verify_password_reset_token` reject the wrong type without changing function signatures.
q3: JWT token-type claim hardening so that access tokens and password-reset tokens signed with the same key cannot be used in place of each other.
Minimal diff, and keep every function signature unchanged.

q2: Optimize `read_items()` in the FastAPI/SQLModel `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` to fetch the count and item list in a single query, and add an Alembic migration in `backend/app/alembic/versions/` creating an `(owner_id, created_at)` index on `Item`.
q3: Paginated item list performance: fetch the count and the page in a single query, and add a composite (owner_id, created_at) index.
FastAPI with SQLModel and an Alembic migration, `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` and `backend/app/alembic/versions/`.
